headlines.title: SoFi’s Earnings Shine While PayPal & Boeing’s Earnings Look “Meh”
headlines.summary: When SoFi's earnings cause the stock to pop more than 15%. Plus, Paypal’s earnings show a company in search of different shareholders.

headlines.title: PayPal’s (PYPL) Turnaround Still Needs Proof
headlines.summary: PayPal’s (PYPL) turnaround still needs more proof, even after its Q3 FY2026 report showed higher adjusted earnings per share (EPS) and an improved full-year outlook. PayPal Holdings operates a global digital-payments network spanning its PayPal and Venmo wallets, branded checkout, Braintree payment processing, credit products, and other merchant services. At the end of 2025, its network connected 440 million active accounts across roughly 200 markets. There is progress.

headlines.title: $10,000 Invested in PayPal 5 Years Ago Is Worth About $2,590 Today. The Company Has Bought Back 8.6% of Its Shares Since January.
headlines.summary: Believing that the stock is undervalued, management has aggressively repurchased shares.

headlines.title: PayPal Holdings (PYPL) Could Be 13% Undervalued On Mixed Third Quarter Earnings
headlines.summary: PayPal Holdings (PYPL) just delivered third quarter earnings that showed basic earnings per share from continuing operations of US$1.26, slightly below the US$1.31 reported for the same period a year earlier. Recent action around PayPal Holdings reflects that mixed picture. The 7.8% one-month share price return and 3.9% seven-day gain suggest that momentum has picked up into and after the earnings release, even though the one-year total shareholder return is still down 9.

headlines.title: American Express vs. PayPal: Which Stock Does Wall Street Expect to Grow Faster Through 2027?
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysAnalysts expect American Express’s normalized EPS to rise 31% from 2025 to 2027, against 11% for PayPal. American Express’s higher forward P/E is backed by that faster growth, which makes it the better buy of the two today.

description: PayPal Holdings, Inc. operates a technology platform that enables digital payments for merchants and consumers worldwide. The company operates a two-sided network at scale that connects merchants and consumers that enables its customers to connect, transact, and send and receive payments through online and in person, as well as transfer and withdraw funds using various funding sources, such as bank accounts, PayPal or Venmo account balance, consumer credit and debit products, credit and debit cards, and cryptocurrencies, as well as other stored value products, including gift cards and eligible rewards. It provides payment solutions under the PayPal, PayPal Credit, Braintree, Venmo, Xoom, Hyperwallet, Honey, and Paidy names. The company was founded in 1998 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.
